title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not by Grothendieck. It is page 7 of a typescript of Robert Steinberg's 'Regular elements of semisimple algebraic groups' (Publ. Math. IHES 25, 1965). It is photographed upside down and was most likely reused as scrap paper: the neighbouring pages are Grothendieck's handwritten notes on Weil q-numbers and on CM fields.

The page contains three things:
(1) The end of Steinberg's introduction, with Theorem 1.10: if k is a perfect field of cohomological dimension ≤ 1 and G is a connected linear group over k, then every conjugacy class of G defined over k contains a k-rational element. It follows from Steinberg's Theorem 1.9, that H^1(k,G)=0 under the same hypotheses, which proves Serre's Conjecture I for perfect fields.
(2) A remark that Kneser had shown H^1(k,G)=0 for G simply connected semisimple over a p-adic field.
(3) The start of §2 'Some recollections'. It fixes notation: k* is the multiplicative group; G_0 is the identity component; G_x is the centralizer of x; x_s and x_u are the Jordan parts; G is semisimple of rank r; T is a maximal torus with an ordered character group; Σ is the root system; X_α is the root subgroup. Item 2.1 begins: X_α is unipotent and isomorphic to the additive group.

Why it may be in the folder: Grothendieck's surrounding notes characterise Weil numbers λ. One criterion is that λ be an eigenvalue of a rational element f ∈ G(Q), where G sits in G_m → G → G_m with compact kernel. Rationality of conjugacy classes (Steinberg) is loosely related to that criterion. Still, the physical presence of the page is most plausibly reuse of paper.
